encoding.name: IDLE
encoding.semantics: No data transfer is required. A Manager uses an IDLE transfer when it does not want to perform a data transfer. Subordinates must always provide a zero-wait OKAY response and the transfer must be ignored.

encoding.name: BUSY
encoding.semantics: Manager continuing a burst but the next transfer cannot take place immediately. Address+control signals must reflect the next transfer in the burst. Subordinates must always provide a zero-wait OKAY response and the transfer must be ignored. BUSY may not end a fixed-length burst.

encoding.name: NONSEQ
encoding.semantics: Single transfer or first transfer of a burst. Address+control are unrelated to the previous transfer. Single transfers on the bus are treated as bursts of length one, so the transfer type is NONSEQUENTIAL.

encoding.name: SEQ
encoding.semantics: Remaining transfers in a burst are SEQUENTIAL and the address is related to the previous transfer. Control information is identical to the previous transfer. Address is equal to the previous address plus the transfer size in bytes (or wraps at the wrap boundary).

encoding.name: Non-cacheable / Non-modifiable
encoding.semantics: Cacheable (Issue A) / Modifiable (Issue B+) bit deasserted.

encoding.name: Cacheable / Modifiable
encoding.semantics: Cacheable (Issue A) / Modifiable (Issue B+) bit asserted.

encoding.name: Data/Inst
encoding.semantics: When asserted indicates a data access; when deasserted indicates an instruction fetch.

encoding.name: Privileged
encoding.semantics: When asserted indicates a privileged access; when deasserted indicates an unprivileged access.

encoding.name: Bufferable
encoding.semantics: If both HPROT[4:3] are deasserted: deasserted -> write response from final destination; asserted -> response can be from intermediate point but write must be visible at final destination in a timely manner.

encoding.name: Modifiable
encoding.semantics: When asserted, the characteristics of the transfer can be modified by the interconnect; when deasserted, they must not be modified.

encoding.name: Lookup
encoding.semantics: When asserted, the transfer must be looked up in a cache; when deasserted, no lookup required and the transfer must propagate to the final destination.

encoding.name: Allocate
encoding.semantics: When asserted, the transfer is recommended to be allocated in the cache; when deasserted, not allocated.

encoding.name: Shareable
encoding.semantics: When asserted, the transfer is to a region shared with other Managers; response must not be provided until the transfer is visible to other Managers. Must be zero for Device memory.

tables.name: Permitted combinations of HPROT bits (Memory type)

encoding.name: Device-nE
encoding.semantics: Device non-Early-write-response. Shareable=0 must be 0 for Device memory.

encoding.name: Write-through, Non/Shareable
encoding.semantics: Cacheable, write-through; Allocate hint per HPROT[5].

encoding.name: Write-back, Non/Shareable
encoding.semantics: Cacheable, write-back; Allocate hint per HPROT[5].

encoding.name: ERROR
encoding.semantics: Access failed. Two-cycle response: cycle 1 HRESP=1+HREADY=0, cycle 2 HRESP=1+HREADY=1.

encoding.name: Instruction access
encoding.semantics: Instruction access (hint, not accurate for all transactions).

encoding.name: Byte lane active
encoding.semantics: Byte lane n of HWDATA carries valid write data.

encoding.name: Byte lane inactive
encoding.semantics: Byte lane n of HWDATA does not carry valid write data (sparse write); not written by Subordinate.

encoding.name: Byte lane active
encoding.semantics: Byte lane n of PWDATA contains valid information.

encoding.name: Byte lane inactive
encoding.semantics: Byte lane n of PWDATA does not carry valid data (write strobes must not be active during a read transfer).

encoding.name: IDLE
encoding.semantics: Default state of the APB. No transfer in progress.

encoding.name: SETUP
encoding.semantics: Transfer required. Lasts exactly one PCLK cycle; unconditional transition to ACCESS on next rising PCLK.

encoding.name: ACCESS
encoding.semantics: Enable phase. PADDR/PWRITE/PSELx/PWDATA/PSTRB/PPROT remain stable. Exit on PREADY=1 (to IDLE or back to SETUP).

ahb_burst_address_equations.Aligned_Address: Manager must align HADDR to (1 << HSIZE) bytes for each transfer in a burst.
ahb_burst_address_equations.WRAP_address_n: HADDR_(n+1) = (HADDR_n + Number_Bytes) modulo Wrap_boundary (mod within the (start_address & ~(Wrap_boundary-1))..+Wrap_boundary range)
ahb_burst_address_equations.INCR_1KB_rule: Incrementing burst must not cross a 1KB address boundary.

evidence.quote: HBURST[2:0]: 0b000 SINGLE, 0b001 INCR, 0b010 WRAP4, 0b011 INCR4, 0b100 WRAP8, 0b101 INCR8, 0b110 WRAP16, 0b111 INCR16.

HPROT[0] Data/Opcode, [1] Privileged, [2] Bufferable, [3] Modifiable, [4] Lookup, [5] Allocate, [6] Shareable. Permitted HPROT[6:2] combinations map to memory types (Device-nE / Device-E / Normal NC / Write-through / Write-back, Non-shareable or Shareable).
Write strobes is an optional feature, which enables a Manager to issue a write that updates only a subset of active write data bytes.

evidence.spec_section: 3.2 Write strobes / Figure 3-3 Byte lane mapping
evidence.quote: The write strobe signals, PSTRB, enable sparse data transfer on the write data bus. ... PSTRB[n] corresponds to PWDATA[(8n+7):8n]. For read transfers the bus master must drive all bits of PSTRB LOW.
IDLE (PSELx=0, PENABLE=0); SETUP (PSELx=1, PENABLE=0); ACCESS (PSELx=1, PENABLE=1).
